units.text: ⟦0⟧1.4 Suppressing Differences Whose Lines All Match a Regular Expression⟦1⟧
units.sourceHTML: 1.4 Suppressing Differences Whose Lines All Match a Regular Expression

units.text: To ignore insertions and deletions of lines that match a ⟦0⟧-style regular expression, use the ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧) option. You should escape regular expressions that contain shell metacharacters to prevent the shell from expanding them. For example, ‘⟦3⟧’ ignores all changes to lines beginning with a digit.
units.sourceHTML: To ignore insertions and deletions of lines that match a grep-style regular expression, use the --ignore-matching-lines=regexp (-I regexp) option. You should escape regular expressions that contain shell metacharacters to prevent the shell from expanding them. For example, ‘diff -I '^[[:digit:]]'’ ignores all changes to lines beginning with a digit.

units.text: However, ⟦0⟧ only ignores the insertion or deletion of lines that contain the regular expression if every changed line in the hunk—every insertion and every deletion—matches the regular expression. In other words, for each nonignorable change, ⟦1⟧ prints the complete set of changes in its vicinity, including the ignorable ones.
units.sourceHTML: However, -I only ignores the insertion or deletion of lines that contain the regular expression if every changed line in the hunk—every insertion and every deletion—matches the regular expression. In other words, for each nonignorable change, diff prints the complete set of changes in its vicinity, including the ignorable ones.

units.text: You can specify more than one regular expression for lines to ignore by using more than one ⟦0⟧ option. ⟦1⟧ tries to match each line against each regular expression.
units.sourceHTML: You can specify more than one regular expression for lines to ignore by using more than one -I option. diff tries to match each line against each regular expression.
